claim_a.claim_text: Deeper backbones (ResNet-101, ResNeXt) yield substantial accuracy gains over shallower ones for dense object detection.
claim_a.evidence_quote: RetinaNet with ResNet-101-FPN achieves 39.1 AP on COCO test-dev, surpassing all published results from both one- and two-stage detectors.

claim_b.claim_text: Joint compound scaling of depth, width, and input resolution is more efficient than scaling depth alone for object detection.
claim_b.evidence_quote: Inspired by recent works ... we propose a compound scaling method for object detectors, which jointly scales up the resolution / depth / width for all backbone, feature network, and box/class prediction networks.

rationale: EfficientDet shows that scaling depth alone (RetinaNet's approach) is suboptimal under FLOP/parameter constraints. The contradiction is in the recommended scaling strategy for the detector designer.
